ȝ[?] Praeterea grauitas adulterij, & mala quae
inde oriuntur expendamus. Periculosius
est & detrimentosius atque peius est adul-
te-rare, quàm furari (quod hodie pauci cre-
dunt, id quod ex supplicijs furum & adultero-
rum intelligitur) adhaec scortatio, mala ani-
mae, corporis, famae & fortunae importat. vt
ex Luc. 15. etiam cognoscere licet, nec non
ex Germanico illo prouerbio: Spiel/ Hu-rey / vnd sauffen / macht

main_text.l: Attenuatur[?] autem hic peccatum furti non
simpliciter, pro quo grauis poena infligitur
secundum legem, sed temporalis & citra mor-
tem, vt scilicet reddat septuplum, id est, plu-
ra quàm abstulit indeterminatè, boues quin-
que pro vno, oues quatuor pro vna, Exod.22.
vel totum quod habet: sed comparatione a-
dulterij longè grauioris, Is enim adulter re-
medium vxoris habet & matrimonij, vel ha-
bere debet, qua incontinentiae medeatur.
Fur vero necessitate compulsus, nempe fa-
mis iniuriam euadere cupiens, deprehensus
vero satisfacit, minori confusioni obnoxius
postea, quàm illi, qui necessitatem patienti
non succurrerunt, in ius traxerunt, spoliave-
runt bonis pauperem, qui non vt ditesceret,
sed vt esurientem stomachum placaret & im-
pleret,

page.notes: The first line opens mid-sentence from the previous page, so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". The paragraph sign before "Praeterea" is a printed ornament that is hard to read; marked [?]. "Attenuatur" and "poena" are doubtful in the scan (the letters look like "Atrenuatur" and "prœna"); marked [?]. The German black letter is set inside roman text and is marked bl. The last word of the page is printed "impleret," with the break marked by an unprinted hyphen, so it is written whole. A printed dot at the lower right and marks at the left edge are not text and are left out.
